title: How Rich Thy Favors, God of Grace
description: How Rich Thy Favors, God of Grace in Tonic Solfa to ST. PETER, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 445 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"Now are we sons of God."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. PETER; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How rich thy fa-vors, God of grace! How var-ious, how di-vine! Full as the o-cean they are poured, And bright as heaven they shine.

lines: How rich thy favors, God of grace!
Full as the ocean they are poured,
And bright as heaven they shine.
To his own palace where he reigns
Jesus, the herald of his love,
Which leads, through sufferings of an hour,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. PETER by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
